page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor, this instance allocates 12 dedicated virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 96.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no bundled local storage and includes a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Dedicated graphics hardware is not present.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-threaded execution. Single-thread processing remains in lower performance percentiles, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 922.0 and reduced throughput during single-threaded compression tests. Conversely, multi-threaded operations reach median industry baselines, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4669.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 38.44 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains steady transfer rates, testing at 56.1 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 48.74 GB/sec for large writes.

Resource allocation delivers strong memory density, making the instance cost-efficient for RAM-demanding tasks that do not require premium per-core execution speeds. The 96.0 GB footprint supports high-concurrency memory pools, demonstrated by 8.52 million Redis SET operations per second and standard database operation scores. Primary operational trade-offs involve modest single-core compute performance, reliance on network-attached block volumes for all storage needs, and a modest 2 Gbps baseline network pipe. The instance is suited for in-memory key-value stores, distributed memory caching, batch ETL processes, and intermediate data processing tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 12 dedicated vCPUs, 6 physical cores, and 96.0 GB of RAM, driven by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server operates under KVM virtualization, includes a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark profiles highlight modest single-thread metrics offset by median-tier multi-threaded throughput and memory speeds, recording 56.1 GB/sec in large-block uncached read tests and 8.52 million Redis SET operations per second. Its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers economical resource density for memory-bound systems where sheer RAM capacity outweighs single-thread instruction speed. The ecs.u0.c1m8.3xlarge is primarily suited for in-memory caching layers, Redis clusters, backend relational database replicas, and memory-intensive extract-transform-load tasks.
